Describe how the codes of a column change over periods

Source: R/describe_codes.R
describe_codes.Rd

Code lists change: municipalities merge, industry codes are revised, a code is retired and a new one takes its place. In a register spanning many years the codes of one column then come and go, and so do errors that look like codes: a typo that occurs in one year, an old code that should have been converted. describe_codes() shows, for every code, the first and last period it occurs in and whether it skips periods in between, and per period how many codes are new and how many are gone. It judges nothing; require a code list with ensure_codes().

Usage

describe_codes(data, code, time, periods = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, or a database or Arrow table: see Database tables in checkpoints.

code

The code column (one column), e.g. municipality.

time

The period column (one column), e.g. year.

periods

Expected periods. Defaults to those observed in data.

Value

An object of class inshape_codes, printed as a summary. It is a list with the counts n_rows, n_codes, n_every_period, n_with_gaps, n_missing (rows with a missing code), n_missing_time and n_outside, the periods, and two tibbles: codes (code, first, last, periods, gaps, rows) and by_period (period, codes, new, gone, missing).

Details

A code that skips periods is usually an error or a conversion applied to some years only. A period with many new and many gone codes is a revision of the code list, and the data before and after it are not comparable without a conversion key.

Missing codes are counted per period, not as a code. In by_period, new is NA in the first period and gone counts the codes last seen in the period before.

Why it is fast

The code and period columns are compressed to integer ids by the compiled hash, and the distinct code-periods are found by one more hash pass. A code column has few distinct values and nearly every row repeats a code-period, so everything else is counted on the code-periods, a few hundred or thousand, not on the millions of rows.

See also

ensure_codes() to require codes from a code list.

Examples

persons <- data.frame(
  year = rep(2018:2021, each = 3),
  municipality = c("955", "956", "957",  "955", "956", "957",
                   "960", "956", "957",  "960", "965", "957")
)
# 955 becomes 960 in 2020 and 956 becomes 965 in 2021
describe_codes(persons, municipality, year)
#> ── Codes: municipality by year ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 12 rows, 5 codes, 4 periods, 2018-2021
#> 
#> • In every period: 1 code (20.0%)
#> • Skipping periods: 0 codes (0.0%)
#> 
#> By period:
#>     period codes   new  gone missing
#>   1   2018     3    NA    NA       0
#>   2   2019     3     0     0       0
#>   3   2020     3     1     1       0
#>   4   2021     3     1     1       0
#> 
#> Codes not in every period, skipping first:
#>     code  first  last periods  gaps  rows
#>   1 965    2021  2021       1     0     1
#>   2 955    2018  2019       2     0     2
#>   3 960    2020  2021       2     0     2
#>   4 956    2018  2020       3     0     3
